material.goal: Produce a comprehensive, source-cited current-state audit of all existing DomainSpec v2 requirements, showing what is implemented, partial, absent, contradictory, superseded, or only planned, and derive the dependency-ordered build remainder without changing implementation or granting acceptance.
material.context: The user corrected a transactional-outbox-only investigation into a whole-DomainSpec audit. Review the complete live DomainSpec requirement and realization corpus: projects/domainspec-v2; implementation/domainspec where live DomainSpec sources reference or depend on it; domainspec-formalization; domainspec-lean-formalization; and repository-local Inventory or telemetry only as discovery/provenance aids. Include language and meta-types, authored relationships, compiler and compiled graph, CLI surfaces including formalize, obligation and certificate emission, generated TypeScript/Python/Rust artifacts, EVF/BTE and conformance, formal Lean refinement, system-integration contracts including transactional outbox, runtime/operational resilience, and production-release requirements. The final status model must keep requirement authority, implementation, test evidence, formal proof, runtime observation, and production readiness separate. Historical plans, accepted reviews, candidates, receipts, and passing focused tests are evidence classes, not automatic implementation or acceptance. All agents are read-only. Only attacks.md and findings.md may be created in the working folder by the parent after join. No source, implementation, plan, decision, ontology, ledger, Inventory, Git, publication, deployment, or external system mutation is authorized.
material.anti_bias_global: declared requirement completeness versus executable compiler and CLI realization versus formal, runtime, and operational evidence completeness

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 will privilege requirement-bearing definitions, decisions, work packs, and lifecycle status, while agent 1 will privilege live compiler, CLI, generator, and test behavior. Agent 0 should expose implemented behavior with no authoritative requirement or stale semantics; agent 1 should expose requirements that never reach an executable path.

Agent 0 will reconstruct the declared product and semantic requirement set, while agent 2 will require hostile witnesses, formal bindings, runtime observations, and production evidence. Agent 0 should expose evidence demands that are not actually required; agent 2 should expose plans or proofs being inflated into end-to-end capability.

Agent 1 will treat executable compiler, CLI, generated artifacts, and focused tests as the strongest implementation evidence, while agent 2 will attack source sensitivity, negative cases, refinement boundaries, failure semantics, and live-runtime closure. Agent 1 should expose purely theoretical gaps already handled in code; agent 2 should expose happy-path implementation that cannot support its stronger claims.

agents.angle: Requirements and authority reconstruction across definitions, relationship families, decisions, roadmaps, work packs, Craft state, formalization claims, and supersession history.
agents.initial_prompt: Act as the requirements-and-authority explorer for dispatch 2026-09-02-domainspec-v2-current-state-completeness-audit. Read the dispatch sheet and the selected portions of strategy-inventory-packet.json, then inspect the live requirement-bearing corpus under projects/domainspec-v2, plus implementation/domainspec, domainspec-formalization, and domainspec-lean-formalization only where referenced by DomainSpec sources. Build an exhaustive requirement catalog grouped by product/release authority; canonical definitions and meta-types; relationship and DS-D8 obligations; authored source and compiled graph; CLI and generation; conformance/evidence; formalization; system integration; runtime/operations; and production release. For each requirement cite the exact current file and selector, identify its owner/status and supersession or contradiction, and distinguish normative requirement, accepted decision, candidate, plan, work-pack task, test expectation, and historical finding. Cross-check the .craft ledger and current roadmaps without treating them as automatic code truth. Return a machine-usable matrix with requirement_id or stable derived ID, family, exact source, authority class, current lifecycle state, dependencies, conflicts, and expected realization/evidence. Explicitly list orphan requirements and implemented behaviors with no current requirement owner. Do not edit files and do not infer acceptance from status words alone.

agents.angle: Executable realization and traceability from authored DomainSpec source through compiler, compiled graph, CLI packages, obligations, certificates, generators, tests, and integration bindings.
agents.initial_prompt: Act as the implementation-traceability explorer for dispatch 2026-09-02-domainspec-v2-current-state-completeness-audit. Read the dispatch sheet and the implementation-relevant entries in strategy-inventory-packet.json, then inspect current source and tests across projects/domainspec-v2/impl and all directly bound definitions, plans, formalization adapters, implementation/domainspec consumers, and generated TypeScript/Python/Rust surfaces. Trace each discovered requirement from authored bytes to parser/schema validation, normalized compiled project graph, semantic checks, DS-D8 obligation IDs/predicates/witnesses, formalize/certificate output, generators, CLI command, hostile/source-sensitivity tests, and conformance receipt where applicable. Run only safe read-only or test commands when needed. Classify each row as BUILT_AND_VERIFIED, BUILT_PARTIAL, DECLARED_ONLY, TEST_ONLY, STALE_OR_CONTRADICTED, or UNKNOWN, with exact paths/selectors and command evidence. Cover every meta-type and relationship family, not only Operation/outbox. Identify dead code, fixture-only behavior, missing CLI exposure, duplicate owners, stale projections, and cross-language parity gaps. Do not edit files, refresh generated bytes, install dependencies, or convert focused test success into runtime or release authority.

agents.angle: Adversarial assurance and end-to-end closure across hostile cases, source sensitivity, Lean refinement, conformance, integration failure semantics, runtime observation, resilience, operability, and production evidence.
agents.initial_prompt: Act as the adversarial evidence-closure explorer for dispatch 2026-09-02-domainspec-v2-current-state-completeness-audit. Read the dispatch sheet and the formalization, integration, resilience, and release leads in strategy-inventory-packet.json, then inspect the current DomainSpec corpus and its direct formal/runtime consumers. Challenge every strong claim with a concrete negative or failure-mode witness. Audit whether TypeScript compiled-graph/projection behavior is actually bound to the Lean CheckedProjectionInput model; whether successful compile universally emits the claimed certificates; whether hostile and source-sensitivity cases cover every admitted DS-D8 family; whether conformance observes real targets or fixtures; and whether system-integration requirements such as atomic state/outbox, unknown commit, retries, idempotency, leases, quarantine, relay/publisher, observability, recovery, deployment, and production gates have concrete implementations and executed evidence. Cover non-outbox runtime and operational requirements as well. Return a failure-mode and evidence matrix with exact sources, observed command results where safe, claim ceiling, missing witness, minimal closure test, and dependency-ordered remediation. Distinguish theorem-in-model, compiler refinement, generated contract, simulated conformance, live runtime observation, and production readiness. Do not edit files or claim that absence from one directory proves global absence without a repository-wide search.
